questions.q: The sex cord arm of the printed tree splits into which two functional groups?
opts: Estrogen producing (feminizing) and androgen producing (virilizing) tumours

questions.q: Name the three androgen producing (virilizing) tumours printed.
opts: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumour, Leydig cell tumour and hilus cell tumour
Sertoli cell tumour, Leydig cell tumour and thecoma
Sertoli-Leydig, granulosa and hilus cell tumours
Leydig cell tumour, hilus cell tumour and fibroma
questions.exp: The virilizing arm lists those three.

questions.q: Reinke's crystals on HPE are printed for which tumour?
questions.exp: The bracket under hilus cell tumour prints '(Reinke's crystals seen on HPE)'.

questions.q: The stromal tumour arm of the tree lists which three tumours?
questions.exp: The stromal column prints fibroma, thecoma, fibrothecoma.

questions.q: Match each tree arm with its printed members - 1) Feminizing 2) Virilizing 3) Stromal ... A) Fibroma, thecoma, fibrothecoma B) Granulosa cell tumour C) Sertoli-Leydig, Leydig and hilus cell tumours ... choose:
questions.exp: The tree prints granulosa as feminizing, the three androgen tumours as virilizing and fibroma-thecoma-fibrothecoma as stromal.

questions.q: Odd one out - which tumour sits in the stromal rather than sex cord arm?
questions.exp: Thecoma is stromal; the rest are sex cord tumours.

questions.q: Sex cord stromal tumours most commonly affect which group?
questions.exp: 'm/c affects perimenopausal women'.

questions.q: Sex cord stromal tumours are printed as which sided?
questions.exp: 'Unilateral' in the features list.

questions.q: Why do sex cord stromal tumours get diagnosed early on the printed page?
opts: Increased sex hormone production causes specific symptoms
questions.exp: 'up Production of sex hormones -> Specific symptoms -> Early diagnosis'.

questions.q: Give the printed prognosis hierarchy across ovarian tumour groups.
opts: Sex cord stromal tumour > GCT > epithelial cell tumour
questions.exp: 'Best prognosis : Sex cord stromal tumor > GCT > Epithelial cell tumor'.

questions.q: True/False: Sex cord stromal tumours are printed as having the best prognosis among the three ovarian tumour groups.
questions.exp: The note prints sex cord stromal first in the hierarchy.

questions.q: Fill up: Increased production of ____ hormones gives sex cord stromal tumours their specific symptoms and early diagnosis.
questions.exp: The chain prints up production of sex hormones.

questions.unit: Granulosa Cell Tumour: Pathophysiology and Presentation

questions.exp: 'Origin : Granulosa cells' in the pathophysiology tree.

questions.unit: Granulosa Cell Tumour: Pathophysiology and Presentation
questions.q: The two tumour markers printed as produced by granulosa cell tumour are:
questions.exp: The produce bracket joins estrogen and inhibin as tumour markers.

questions.unit: Granulosa Cell Tumour: Pathophysiology and Presentation

questions.exp: 'Antimullerian hormone (At puberty)'.

questions.unit: Granulosa Cell Tumour: Pathophysiology and Presentation
questions.q: Excessive bleeding in granulosa cell tumour presents as which two printed patterns?
opts: Atypical uterine bleeding (perimenopausal) and post-menopausal bleeding
Atypical uterine bleeding and intermenstrual bleeding
questions.exp: The bleeding bullets print atypical uterine bleeding (perimenopausal) and post-menopausal bleeding.

questions.unit: Granulosa Cell Tumour: Pathophysiology and Presentation
questions.q: In a pre-pubertal girl, granulosa cell tumour presents as:
questions.exp: 'Precocious puberty' in the presentation list.

questions.unit: Granulosa Cell Tumour: Pathophysiology and Presentation
questions.q: Because of its link with endometrial cancer, which step is mandatory in all granulosa cases?
questions.exp: 'Endometrial cancer : Endometrial sampling mandatory in all cases'.

questions.unit: Granulosa Cell Tumour: Pathophysiology and Presentation
questions.q: The note box lists which two ovarian cancers associated with endometrial cancer?
opts: Endometroid tumour and granulosa cell tumour
Clear cell tumour and granulosa cell tumour
Endometroid tumour and clear cell tumour
questions.exp: The box prints a. Endometroid tumor b. Granulosa cell tumor.

questions.unit: Granulosa Cell Tumour: Pathophysiology and Presentation
questions.q: Match each granulosa attribute with its printed value - 1) Origin 2) Gene 3) Markers 4) Mandatory step ... A) Estrogen and inhibin B) Granulosa cells C) Endometrial sampling D) FOX L-2 ... choose:
questions.exp: Origin granulosa cells, gene FOX L-2, markers estrogen and inhibin, mandatory endometrial sampling.

questions.unit: Granulosa Cell Tumour: Pathophysiology and Presentation
questions.q: Scenario: A 52-year-old with post-menopausal bleeding has a unilateral solid-cystic ovarian mass and thickened endometrium. The printed tumour and mandatory step are:
opts: Granulosa cell tumour with endometrial sampling
questions.exp: Post-menopausal bleeding with an estrogenic ovarian mass fits granulosa cell tumour, and endometrial sampling is mandatory.

questions.q: The HPE hallmark printed for granulosa cell tumour is:
questions.exp: 'HPE : Call Exner body' on page 258.

questions.q: The Call Exner body is drawn as:
opts: Central acidophilic material surrounded by follicle like cells, with coffee bean nuclei
Central capillaries surrounded by tumour cells
Nests of cells with lymphocytic septa
questions.exp: The figure label prints central acidophilic material surrounded by follicle like cells + coffee bean nuclei.

questions.q: Coffee bean nuclei accompany which two printed tumours?
opts: Granulosa cell tumour and clear cell tumour
Granulosa cell tumour and Brenner's tumour
questions.exp: Page 254 note 1 and page 258 both pair coffee bean nuclei with granulosa and Brenner's.

questions.q: True/False: The Call Exner body contains central acidophilic material surrounded by follicle-like cells.
questions.exp: The figure label prints exactly that description.

questions.q: Odd one out - which HPE feature belongs to yolk sac tumour rather than granulosa cell tumour?
questions.exp: Schiller Duval bodies are the yolk sac hallmark of page 256.

questions.q: Fibroma is printed as which combination?
questions.exp: 'U/L, benign, solid tumor' under fibroma features.

questions.q: The HPE of fibroma shows:
questions.exp: 'HPE : Well differentiated fibroblasts'.

questions.q: Fibroma is associated with which syndrome?
questions.exp: 'Associated with meig's syndrome'.

questions.q: Meig's syndrome is printed as the triad of which tumours with ascites and pleural effusion?
opts: Fibroma, thecoma, Brenner's tumour or granulosa cell
questions.exp: The Meig's cell prints fibroma/thecoma/Brenner's/granulosa cell + ascites + pleural effusion.

questions.q: The defining behaviour of true Meig's syndrome after tumour removal is:
opts: Resolution of ascites and pleural effusion
questions.exp: 'Removal of tumor -> Resolution of ascites and pleural effusion'.

questions.q: Pseudo-meig's syndrome is printed as ascites with pleural effusion due to:
opts: Any other ovarian tumour (mucinous cystadenoma) or any other condition (fibroid)
questions.exp: The pseudo column prints any other ovarian tumour (mucinous cystadenoma) or any other condition (fibroid).

questions.q: Match each syndrome with its printed tumour set - 1) Meig's 2) Pseudo-meig's ... A) Mucinous cystadenoma or fibroid with ascites and effusion B) Fibroma, thecoma, Brenner's or granulosa with ascites and effusion ... choose:
questions.exp: True Meig's uses the four sex cord/stromal tumours; pseudo uses any other tumour or condition.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman with a fibroid develops ascites and pleural effusion that resolve after hysterectomy. The printed label is:
questions.exp: Fibroid as the cause places it in the pseudo-meig's column.

questions.q: Fill up: Removal of the tumour in Meig's syndrome leads to ____ of ascites and pleural effusion.
questions.exp: The arrow prints resolution of ascites and pleural effusion.

questions.q: True/False: Fibroma is printed as a bilateral malignant cystic tumour.
opts: False - it is bilateral benign solid
False - it is unilateral malignant solid
questions.exp: The features print U/L, benign, solid.

questions.q: Name the three printed primary sources of metastatic ovarian tumours.
questions.exp: The bracket lists stomach (m/c), GIT and breast carcinoma.

questions.q: The most common primary source printed is:
questions.exp: 'Stomach (m/c)' heads the list.

questions.q: The two spread routes printed to the ovary are:
questions.exp: The arrow label prints retrograde lymphatics/transcoelomic spread.

questions.q: Match each printed source with its rank - 1) Stomach 2) GIT 3) Breast carcinoma ... A) m/c B) Second listed C) Third listed ... choose:
questions.exp: Stomach is labelled m/c and the list order is stomach, GIT, breast.

questions.q: Krukenberg tumour arises from which primary site and end?
questions.exp: The line prints 'Stomach cancer (Pyloric end)'.

questions.q: The route printed for Krukenberg tumour is:
questions.exp: The arrow label prints retrograde lymphatics.

questions.q: Krukenberg tumour is bilateral in what percentage?
questions.exp: '80% : B/L' under features.

questions.q: The ovarian enlargement in Krukenberg tumour is described as:
questions.exp: 'Symmetric enlargement of ovaries'.

questions.q: What is retained in Krukenberg tumour despite metastasis?
questions.exp: 'Shape & capsule of ovary : Retained'.

questions.q: The consistency and mobility printed for Krukenberg tumour are:
questions.exp: 'Mobile + waxy consistency'.

questions.q: The HPE hallmark of Krukenberg tumour is:
questions.exp: 'HPE : Signet ring cells'.

questions.q: The signet ring appearance is produced by:
opts: Glycogen filled cytoplasm pushing the nucleus centrally
Mucin filled nucleus pushing cytoplasm aside
Mucin filled cytoplasm pushing the nucleus to one side
questions.exp: The sub-bullet prints mucin filled cytoplasm pushes nucleus to one side.

questions.q: Match each Krukenberg feature with its printed value - 1) Primary end 2) Route 3) Bilaterality 4) HPE ... A) Signet ring cells B) Pyloric end C) 80% bilateral D) Retrograde lymphatics ... choose:
questions.exp: Pyloric end primary, retrograde lymphatics, 80% bilateral and signet ring cells.

questions.q: Scenario: A 50-year-old with a gastric pyloric carcinoma develops bilateral symmetric solid ovarian masses retaining ovarian shape. The printed diagnosis is:
questions.exp: The stomach pyloric end with retrograde lymphatic spread defines Krukenberg tumour.

questions.q: Odd one out - which feature contradicts the printed Krukenberg profile?
questions.exp: The page prints 80% bilateral, not unilateral.

questions.q: True/False: Transcoelomic spread is one of the two printed routes by which stomach, GIT and breast secondaries reach the ovary.
questions.exp: The bracket arrow prints retrograde lymphatics/transcoelomic spread.

questions.q: Stage 1 in the printed ovarian FIGO table means:
questions.exp: The stage 1 row prints 'Limited to ovary'.

questions.q: Stage IA is printed as:
questions.exp: The IA row prints one ovary involved.

questions.q: Stage IB is printed as:
questions.exp: The IB row prints both ovaries involved.

questions.q: The intact capsule label spans which substages?
questions.exp: The merged cell 'Intact capsule' covers the IA and IB rows.

questions.q: Stage IC is defined by:
questions.exp: The IC row prints capsule ruptured with three sub-arms.

questions.q: Match the IC substage with its printed cause - 1) IC1 2) IC2 3) IC3 ... A) Preoperative rupture B) Malignant ascites C) Intraoperative rupture ... choose:
questions.exp: IC1 is intraoperative rupture, IC2 preoperative rupture and IC3 malignant ascites.

questions.q: Stage 2 in the printed table means spread to:
questions.exp: The stage 2 row prints spreads to other pelvic organs.

questions.q: Stage 2A involves which organs?
questions.exp: The 2A row prints fallopian tube or uterus.

questions.q: Stage 2B involves which organs?
questions.exp: The 2B row prints bladder, rectum.

questions.q: Stage 3 in the printed table means spread:
questions.exp: The stage 3 row prints spreads beyond pelvis into abdomen.

questions.q: Stage 3A1 is defined by involvement of:
questions.exp: The 3A1 line prints retroperitoneal lymph nodes involved.

questions.q: Stage 3A2 is defined by:
questions.exp: The 3A2 line prints microscopic involvement above pelvic brim.

questions.q: Stage 3B implant size printed is:
opts: Macroscopic implants <= 2 cm above pelvic brim
questions.exp: The 3B row prints macroscopic involvement above pelvic brim with size of implant <= 2 cm.

questions.q: Stage 3C implant size printed is:
opts: Macroscopic implants >= 2 cm above pelvic brim
questions.exp: The 3C row prints >= 2 cm.

questions.q: The plus-minus extension to liver and spleen capsule or surface belongs to which substages?
questions.exp: The merged cell spans the 3B and 3C rows.

questions.q: Stage 4 in the printed table means:
questions.exp: The stage 4 row prints distant metastasis.

questions.q: Stage 4A is printed as:
questions.exp: The 4A row prints malignant pleural effusion.

questions.q: Stage 4B is printed as:
opts: Liver/spleen parenchyma involved or inguinal lymph node involved
questions.exp: The 4B row prints liver/spleen parenchyma involved OR inguinal lymph node involved.

questions.q: Match each stage with its printed definition - 1) IC3 2) 2B 3) 3A1 4) 4A ... A) Bladder and rectum B) Malignant pleural effusion C) Malignant ascites D) Retroperitoneal nodes ... choose:
questions.exp: IC3 is malignant ascites, 2B bladder and rectum, 3A1 retroperitoneal nodes and 4A malignant pleural effusion.

questions.q: Scenario: At laparotomy an ovarian cancer capsule ruptures while removing the mass; peritoneum is otherwise clean. The printed substage is:
questions.exp: Intraoperative rupture is IC1.

questions.q: Scenario: Cytology of pleural fluid shows malignant cells in a woman with ovarian cancer. The printed stage is:
questions.exp: Malignant pleural effusion defines 4A.

questions.q: Odd one out - which finding is NOT stage 4B on the printed table?
questions.exp: Pleural effusion is 4A; the parenchymal and inguinal findings are 4B.

questions.q: Involvement of bladder and rectum is staged in ovarian cancer as:
questions.exp: The note prints ovarian cancer : 2B for bladder and rectum.

questions.q: The same bladder or rectum involvement in other gynaecological cancers is staged as:
questions.exp: The note prints other gynaecological cancers : 4A.

questions.q: True/False: Bladder mucosal involvement upstages ovarian cancer to 4A just as in cervical cancer.
opts: False - it is stage 3B in ovary
False - it is stage 4B in ovary
questions.exp: The note prints ovarian cancer 2B against 4A for other gynaecological cancers.

questions.q: Match the organ involvement with its printed stage in each cancer - 1) Bladder/rectum in ovarian cancer 2) Bladder/rectum in other gynae cancers ... A) 4A B) 2B ... choose:
questions.exp: The note splits the same finding into 2B for ovary and 4A for others.

questions.q: How many steps of surgical staging are printed?
questions.exp: The numbered table runs 1 to 7.

questions.q: Step 1 of surgical staging is:
questions.exp: Row 1 prints midline incision.

questions.q: If ascites is present at step 2, the printed action is:
opts: Ascitic fluid sample sent for cytology
questions.exp: The plus arm prints ascitic fluid sample sent for cytology.

questions.q: If no ascites is present at step 2, the printed action is:
opts: Saline wash done and sent for cytology
questions.exp: The minus arm prints saline wash done & sent for cytology.

questions.q: Step 3 of surgical staging is:
opts: Inspection + palpation of all abdominal organs
questions.exp: Row 3 prints inspection + palpation of all abdominal organs.

questions.q: Step 4 of surgical staging is:
questions.exp: Row 4 prints multiple peritoneal biopsies taken.

questions.q: Step 5 of surgical staging is:
questions.exp: Row 5 prints Type 1 TAH + BSO.

questions.q: Step 6 of surgical staging is:
questions.exp: Row 6 prints infracolic omentectomy.

questions.q: Step 7 of surgical staging is:
opts: Pelvic & para-aortic lymph node dissection followed by closure
questions.exp: Row 7 prints pelvic & para-aortic lymph node dissection then P/b then closure.

questions.q: Arrange the surgical staging steps in printed order - 1) Infracolic omentectomy 2) Midline incision 3) Peritoneal biopsies 4) Cytology of ascites or wash 5) Inspection and palpation 6) TAH + BSO 7) Node dissection ... choose:
questions.exp: The table order is incision, cytology, inspection, biopsies, TAH + BSO, omentectomy, node dissection.

questions.q: Fill up: When ascites is absent, a ____ wash is done and sent for cytology at step 2.
questions.exp: The minus arm prints saline wash.

questions.q: True/False: The omentectomy printed in surgical staging is infracolic.
questions.exp: Row 6 prints infracolic omentectomy.

questions.q: The surgery of choice printed for ovarian cancer is:
opts: TAH + BSO (total abdominal hysterectomy + bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy)
questions.exp: 'Surgery of choice : TAH (Total abdominal hysterectomy) + BSO (Bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy)'.

questions.q: Conservative surgery is printed as:
questions.exp: 'Conservative Sx : U/L salpingo-oophorectomy (without hysterectomy)'.

questions.q: Conservative surgery is indicated for GCT in which age band?
questions.exp: 'GCT : 10-30 yrs of age'.

questions.q: Conservative surgery for sex cord tumours is indicated in:
questions.exp: 'Sex cord tumors : Young females'.

questions.q: Conservative surgery for epithelial tumours is indicated in which stage with what family status?
opts: Stage IC with family not complete
Stage IA with family not complete
Stage IIA with family not complete
questions.exp: 'Stage IA epithelial tumor + family not complete'.

questions.q: Debulking surgery is printed for which stages?
questions.exp: 'Debulking Sx : Advanced stages (Stages 3, 4)'.

questions.q: Match each surgery with its printed indication - 1) TAH + BSO 2) Conservative U/L salpingo-oophorectomy 3) Debulking ... A) Stages 3 and 4 B) Surgery of choice C) GCT 10-30 yrs, young sex cord cases, stage IA epithelial with incomplete family ... choose:
questions.exp: TAH + BSO is the default, conservative surgery serves the fertility group and debulking serves advanced disease.

questions.q: Scenario: A 17-year-old with stage IA dysgerminoma wants children. The printed operation is:
questions.exp: GCT at 10-30 yrs with stage IA epithelial-equivalent fertility criteria prints conservative U/L salpingo-oophorectomy.

questions.q: True/False: Conservative surgery retains the uterus while removing the affected tube and ovary.
opts: False - it retains the ovary too
questions.exp: The bracket prints without hysterectomy after U/L salpingo-oophorectomy.

questions.q: Epithelial cell tumours receive how many cycles of chemotherapy?
questions.exp: The epithelial column prints 6 cycles.

questions.q: The routes printed for epithelial chemotherapy are:
questions.exp: The cell prints IV + Intraperitoneal.

questions.q: The drugs printed for epithelial cell tumours are:
questions.exp: The cell prints paclitaxel + carboplatin/cisplatin.

questions.q: Chemotherapy for epithelial tumours is indicated in which stages?
opts: All stages except stage IA and IB
questions.exp: The indication row prints all stages except stage IA and IB.

questions.q: The BEP regimen printed for germ cell tumours expands to:
questions.exp: The GCT column prints B bleomycin, E etoposide, P cisplatin.

questions.q: Germ cell tumour chemotherapy is omitted in which situation?
questions.exp: The indication row prints all stages except dysgerminoma stage 1 (best prognosis).

questions.q: Sex cord stromal tumours need chemotherapy only in which stages?
questions.exp: The indication row prints chemotherapy needed only in stage 3 and 4.

questions.q: The regimen printed for sex cord stromal tumours is:
questions.exp: The sex cord column prints the same BEP trio.

questions.q: Match each tumour group with its printed chemotherapy rule - 1) Epithelial 2) Germ cell 3) Sex cord stromal ... A) BEP in all stages except dysgerminoma stage 1 B) 6 cycles IV + IP paclitaxel with carboplatin/cisplatin except IA and IB C) BEP only in stages 3 and 4 ... choose:
questions.exp: Epithelial gets six cycles except IA/IB, GCT gets BEP except stage 1 dysgerminoma and sex cord only in stages 3-4.

questions.q: Scenario: A stage IB epithelial ovarian cancer has been fully staged and operated. The printed adjuvant plan is:
opts: 6 cycles of IV + intraperitoneal paclitaxel with carboplatin
questions.exp: The indication row exempts stage IA and IB from epithelial chemotherapy.

questions.q: Scenario: The same table for a stage IC epithelial ovarian cancer prints which adjuvant plan?
opts: 6 cycles of IV + intraperitoneal paclitaxel with carboplatin or cisplatin
questions.exp: Stage IC lies outside the IA/IB exemption, so the six-cycle IV + IP regimen applies.

questions.q: Fill up: The P of the BEP regimen printed for germ cell and sex cord tumours is ____.
questions.exp: Both columns print P : Cisplatin.

questions.q: True/False: Stage IA epithelial ovarian cancer receives post-operative chemotherapy on the printed table.
questions.exp: The indication row exempts stage IA and IB.

questions.q: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumour is printed as which type of ovarian tumour?
questions.exp: The note prints 'Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor : Androgen secreting ovarian tumor'.

questions.q: Name the four printed virilization features of Sertoli-Leydig cell tumour.
opts: Hirsutism, acne, deep voice and clitoral atrophy
Hirsutism, baldness, breast atrophy and enlarged clitoris
Hirsutism, acne, baldness and enlarged clitoris
Acne, baldness, hirsutism and vaginal atrophy
questions.exp: The bullets print hirsutism, acne, baldness and enlarged clitoris (virilization).

questions.q: The printed label for enlarged clitoris in this note is:
questions.exp: The bracket prints '(Virilization)' after enlarged clitoris.

questions.q: Match each virilizing presentation with the printed tumour that causes it - 1) Hirsutism with acne, baldness and clitoromegaly 2) Precocious puberty or post-menopausal bleeding 3) Reinke's crystals on HPE ... A) Hilus cell tumour B) Sertoli-Leydig cell tumour C) Granulosa cell tumour ... choose:
questions.exp: The androgen note ties virilization to Sertoli-Leydig cell tumour, bleeding patterns to granulosa cell tumour and Reinke's crystals to hilus cell tumour.

questions.q: Scenario: A 24-year-old with an ovarian mass presents with new hirsutism, acne and clitoromegaly. The printed tumour is:
questions.exp: The note ties the androgen-secreting virilizing picture to Sertoli-Leydig cell tumour.

questions.q: Odd one out - which feature is NOT in the printed Sertoli-Leydig virilization list?
questions.exp: Post-menopausal bleeding belongs to the estrogenic granulosa presentation.
